name: FVG_REVERSION
what_was_tested: FVG_REVERSION v1.0.0 (bullish/bearish gap-touch reversion, MA200 trend filter, ATR-based stop/target) across 7 crypto assets x {2h, 4h, 12h} = 21 configs, 70/30 chronological split, bootstrap CI + random-entry baseline.
why_it_died: 18 of 21 configs DIED, 0 SURVIVED. Died on every single 2h and 4h config across all 7 assets. Even the 3 PROMISING-WATCHLIST configs (all 12h) showed a near-zero edge over random-entry timing (+0.00 to +0.03 R) - the gap-touch trigger itself wasn't adding meaningful value beyond randomly-timed entries in the same trend regime.

name: FVG_REVERSION (cross-asset extension)
what_was_tested: The identical FVG_REVERSION v1.0.0 logic re-tested against every other asset class this project covers, extending the original crypto-only verdict above: 6 metals configs (SILVER, PLATINUM x 2h/4h/12h), 30 forex configs (10 pairs x {1h,4h,1day,1week}), and ~90 stock configs (27 stocks + 3 index ETFs x 4 timeframes).
why_it_died: DIED on effectively every additional config tested. All 6 metals configs DIED (every train half negative, several with a CI clearing zero on the negative side). All 30 forex configs DIED outright - every pair, every timeframe. Stocks showed only 9 of 90 configs reaching PROMISING-WATCHLIST (81 DIED). Four independent asset-class tests all confirm the same crypto-native finding: the gap-touch trigger carries no durable edge anywhere this project has looked.

name: BOS_CONTINUATION
what_was_tested: BOS_CONTINUATION v1.0.0 (structure-break continuation, MA200 trend filter, ATR-capped structural stop) across 7 crypto assets x {4h, 12h, 24h} = 21 configs, 70/30 chronological split, bootstrap CI + random-entry baseline.
why_it_died: 0 of 21 configs SURVIVED the strict bar. 13 are PROMISING-WATCHLIST, but roughly half of all (asset, timeframe, half) cells showed a NEGATIVE edge over random-entry timing - most of the apparent promise looks attributable to the MA200 regime filter, not the structure-break trigger itself. The capped 3.0x ATR stop (not the structural swing-point stop) was used in 75-95% of trades across almost every config.

name: FUNDING_EXTREME
what_was_tested: FUNDING_EXTREME v1.0.0 (contrarian, long-only entries on crowded-short funding-rate extremes) across BTC/ETH/SOL/BNB x {8h, 24h} = 8 configs, 70/30 chronological split, bootstrap CI + random-entry baseline.
why_it_died: No asset/timeframe combination showed a robust, cross-validated edge. Three test halves were statistically significantly NEGATIVE (ETH/8h, SOL/8h, SOL/24h). The single strongest result (BNB/8h train) was never confirmed by its own 12-trade test half.

name: EMA-trail exit (v2 A/B variants)
what_was_tested: Armed-EMA trailing-stop exit variants of both single-asset live survivors (BNB/12h TREND_PULLBACK-trail: EMA21, GOLD/1week BREAKOUT_MOMENTUM-trail: EMA8), identical entries and disaster stops to v1, compared side by side through the upgraded harness.
why_it_died: The trail's asymmetric win/loss shape (bigger winners, smaller losers, higher profit factor, lower drawdown) showed up clearly in-sample on both configs, but did not survive to the test half on either: BNB's test expectancy flipped negative under the trail (v1 stayed positive); GOLD's test expectancy stayed positive but was weaker than v1's, with a confidence interval that no longer cleared zero.

name: TREND_PULLBACK filter variants (FVG-overlap, BOS-recency)
what_was_tested: Two filtered variants of the live BNB/12h TREND_PULLBACK survivor - one requiring an overlapping open Fair Value Gap in the last 10 candles, one requiring a Break of Structure within the last 20 candles - compared against unfiltered v1 on identical data.
why_it_died: The BOS filter was a complete no-op: identical results to v1 in every metric on both halves - it never once rejected a trade v1 would have taken on this data. The FVG filter roughly halved the sample and made test-half expectancy worse than v1's (0.095R vs 0.243R) on a sample too small to trust either way. Neither filter raised per-trade quality.

name: LEADLAG_FOLLOW
what_was_tested: BTC-to-altcoin Granger-causality lead-lag following (BTC-SOL lag5, BTC-XRP lag3, BTC-DOGE lag3, BTC-NEAR lag5, all 12h) re-tested for robustness across shifted candle grids (native, +3h, +6h offsets).
why_it_died: All 4 pairs passed the original native-grid train/test filter but failed the grid-shift robustness check on at least one shifted grid - BTC-XRP failed on every shifted grid tested, and the other three each flipped negative on at least one offset.

name: MEAN_REVERSION variants (relaxed-pullback, deep-value)
what_was_tested: Relaxed-pullback (BTC/12h, BNB/12h) and deep-value (XRP/2h, NEAR/2h) MEAN_REVERSION variants re-tested for robustness across shifted candle grids.
why_it_died: Every one of these configs passed its original native-grid train/test filter but flipped negative on at least one shifted grid offset - none held up as a robust, grid-independent edge once the candle grid's wall-clock alignment was perturbed.

name: MACRO_RISK_ON
what_was_tested: Dollar-proxy (UUP/DXY/EUR-USD cascade) + FRED DFII10 real-yield regime-following strategy on BTC and GOLD, full available daily history, 70/30 chronological split.
why_it_died: BTC's expectancy flipped from +0.191R (train) to -0.140R (test). GOLD's train half was itself negative (-0.019R) before the test half even mattered (+0.018R). Neither asset passed the strict positive-both-halves filter.

name: MACRO_RISK_ON (metals extension: SILVER/PLATINUM)
what_was_tested: The same dollar-proxy + DFII10 regime logic re-tested on SILVER and PLATINUM/24h during Asset Expansion Phase A, alongside 8 other strategy families.
why_it_died: PLATINUM DIED outright (train ExpR +0.210 flipped to -0.061 in test). SILVER reached PROMISING-WATCHLIST (train N=158 ExpR=0.051, test N=94 ExpR=0.162) but its test-half CI still crosses zero, and it was NOT among the 5 SILVER configs ultimately selected for live paper-tracking wiring - a mixed, unconvincing result on the one metal that didn't die outright.

name: MACRO_RISK_ON (stocks extension: SPY/QQQ/IWM)
what_was_tested: The same regime logic applied to the 3 major index ETFs (SPY, QQQ, IWM) during the Comprehensive Asset Expansion Stocks task - the natural bias-free universe for a broad macro-regime signal.
why_it_died: SPY DIED (train negative, test barely positive). IWM DIED the same way. Only QQQ reached PROMISING-WATCHLIST (train N=159 ExpR=0.010, test N=102 ExpR=0.076) - the best-sampled of the three, but the expectancy itself is thin. 2 of 3 index ETFs show no edge at all; the one exception is weak.

name: MACRO_RISK_ON (forex extension: EUR/USD, USD/JPY)
what_was_tested: The same regime logic applied to EUR/USD and USD/JPY at 1day during the Comprehensive Asset Expansion Forex task.
why_it_died: Both pairs DIED outright with both train AND test strongly negative (EUR/USD: -0.168/-0.204 ExpR; USD/JPY: -0.171/-0.064 ExpR) - a clean, uniform failure with no ambiguity, matching FVG_REVERSION's own clean forex failure in the same batch.

name: MACRO_RISK_ON (PSX extension: HBL)
what_was_tested: A Pakistan-adapted regime variant (USD/PKR + WTI oil in place of the dollar-proxy/DFII10 pair) applied to HBL, the one PSX ticker that cleared the corporate-action guard in the PSX Strategy Sweep.
why_it_died: DIED with a genuinely adequate sample (train N=216 ExpR=-0.053, test N=112 ExpR=+0.092) - not a thin, inconclusive result, a real negative one on real sample size. OGDC and LUCK could not even be tested (both halted by the corporate-action guard before a backtest could run).

name: CARRY_MOMENTUM
what_was_tested: CARRY_MOMENTUM v1.0.0 (rank-and-select the top-3 forex pairs by interest-rate differential among momentum-passing candidates) across all 7 audited forex pairs, {1day, 1week}, 70/30 chronological split.
why_it_died: Both timeframes DIED with an adequate, well-sampled negative result - not a thin one. 1day's train-half CI is entirely negative ([-0.211, -0.041], N=653) and clears the 20-trade bar by a wide margin on both halves. Edge over random was negative in 3 of 4 half-configs: ranking by rate differential performed WORSE than picking randomly among momentum-passing candidates. STOP dominated the exit mix everywhere (roughly half of all positions), consistent with a momentum filter that wasn't actually confirming the carry was durable.

name: RANGE_MEAN_REVERSION variant experiments (EUR/USD 4h long-only, ETH 4h adx-falling)
what_was_tested: Four RMR variant hypotheses tested against fresh baselines on identical data: RMR_LONG_ONLY_EURUSD_4H, RMR_ADX_FALLING_ETH_4H, RMR_LONG_ONLY_BTC_1D, RMR_CONFIRMATION_BTC_1D. A follow-up Stage 3 refinement then applied the already-registered long-only filter to ETH specifically, to test whether its own weakness was also short-side driven.
why_it_died: RMR_LONG_ONLY_EURUSD_4H stayed DIED (improved over baseline, but still negative). RMR_ADX_FALLING_ETH_4H stayed DIED (test flipped positive but train worsened - an inconsistent, non-robust pattern). The Stage 3 ETH refinement DIED outright, refuting the long-only hypothesis for ETH specifically - this was also the ONE config in the entire cycle genuinely eligible for grid-shift testing (crypto's continuous trading has no structural gap blocking it), and it didn't even reach the point of qualifying for that test. Only the BTC/1d variants (long-only, confirmation) reached PROMISING-WATCHLIST, and even a Stage 3 attempt to stack both BTC filters together only shrank the sample further without improving the result.

name: REGIME_TRANSITION
what_was_tested: A new strategy built on RANGE_MEAN_REVERSION's own regime concept: does trading the regime CHANGE itself (a mature range ending) work, rather than trading inside the range as RMR does? Full state machine (mature-range detection, ceiling/floor stop, range-height target, failed-transition exit), swept across 14 asset/timeframe configs with a bespoke random-entry baseline isolating the boundary-break trigger.
why_it_died: 11 of 14 configs DIED, 0 SURVIVED. The 3 PROMISING-WATCHLIST configs (ETH/4h, ETH/1d, EURUSD/1d) all carry a LOW SAMPLE flag on at least one half - this mechanism (a 10-candle mature range followed by a qualifying transition) is low-frequency by construction on every timeframe tested, and 0 configs reached the grid-shift qualifying bar. The mechanism works exactly as designed (30 passing unit tests); the live-market signal is not yet distinguishable from noise at the sample sizes available.

name: RANGE_MATURITY gate
what_was_tested: A single new gate bolted onto RANGE_MEAN_REVERSION v1.0.0 (unchanged otherwise): entry requires ADX<25 for >= N consecutive closed candles beforehand (N=20 for 4h/1d, N=8 for 1week) - testing whether range AGE was the missing variable behind RMR's own thin results. Compared against fresh v1.0.0 baselines across 7 targeted configs.
why_it_died: The gate never rescued a single DIED baseline, and it actively WORSENED GOLD/1week - RMR's single best result across the whole project - flipping train-half expectancy from +0.026 to -0.038. SILVER/1week is the one config that held its PROMISING-WATCHLIST status under the gate, but with a smaller sample (23->18 train, 15->11 test) and a smaller edge (train ExpR 0.320->0.187), the same 'shrinks without concentrating' signature that already counted as evidence against a robust effect elsewhere in this project. Range age is not the missing variable.

name: REGIME_ALLOCATOR (ADX-gating existing survivors)
what_was_tested: ADX(14)>=20-gated, append-only new versions of two already-verified, LIVE survivors (BREAKOUT_MOMENTUM GOLD/1week, TREND_PULLBACK BNB/12h), each compared against a fresh ungated baseline on identical data - testing whether regime-gating improves strategies that already work.
why_it_died: Neither config's classification changed under gating (GOLD/1week stayed SURVIVED; BNB/12h stayed PROMISING-WATCHLIST). Gating traded away roughly 10% of the sample for a marginal, split-direction shift in expectancy (worse train, better test, on BOTH configs) - not the consistent, both-halves improvement a genuine regime-gating effect would produce. A clean null result: regime-gating neither helps nor meaningfully hurts either survivor, so simplicity wins and neither live registration was touched.

name: Vol-Clustering position-size multiplier (H2)
what_was_tested: A volatility-clustering-based position-size multiplier (scales risk_per_trade up during high-cluster-score periods) applied to 7 configs across all 3 asset classes tested in this project: crypto (GOLD/1week BREAKOUT_MOMENTUM, BNB/12h TREND_PULLBACK), stocks (INTU/1day MEAN_REVERSION, NVDA/1week and AAPL/1week BREAKOUT_MOMENTUM), and forex (EUR/JPY/1week BREAKOUT_MOMENTUM, EUR/JPY/1day BOS_CONTINUATION).
why_it_died: Not a backtest failure but a mathematical one: R-multiple expectancy and win-rate are PROVABLY invariant to this multiplier everywhere (it scales risk_dollars and net_pnl by the same factor, so their ratio - the R-multiple - cannot change; confirmed exactly 0.0 or floating-point noise across all 7 configs, 3 asset classes, 4 strategy families). Max drawdown WORSENS in 6 of 7 configs. Net dollar P&L improves in 6 of 7, but this is leverage amplifying whatever the underlying trade sequence already contained, not evidence of skill or edge. Not recommended for production deployment as a live position-sizing enhancement.

name: LIQUIDATION_PREDICTOR
what_was_tested: A data-availability audit for a proposed liquidation-cascade prediction strategy, checking for any free, pollable, keyless REST liquidation feed across major crypto exchanges - never reached strategy code or backtesting.
why_it_died: BLOCKED-ON-DATA before any strategy could be built: Binance's public liquidation feed is discontinued, Bybit v5 has no equivalent route, OKX was inconclusive (DNS failure from the test environment, would need re-testing from a different network), and Coinalyze requires a paid-tier-style registered API key this project doesn't have. No strategy code was written - only the audit is committed, exactly as intended for a data-blocked hypothesis.

name: REPAIR_BREAKOUT_QUALITY
what_was_tested: A user-supplied external spec (display name FIX_BREAKOUT_QUALITY): 4H long-only breakout above the prior 30-candle high, MA200/MA20>MA200 trend support, ATR/close<=4%, a multi-candle retest confirmation (entry deferred to the candle AFTER a later candle retests and closes back above the breakout level), 1.0x-ATR stop with no gap tolerance (a candle closing through the stop defers the exit to the next candle's open rather than fictionally filling at the stop price), fixed 1.5R target. Tested fresh via Vatican's own harness (70/30 chronological split, bootstrap CI, random-entry baseline, exhaustive 4-offset grid-shift) across BTC/XRP/BNB, last 3 years of native 4H candles - the external testers' own 12-trade, +0.158R stats were never reused as evidence.
why_it_died: DIED on all 3 assets: BTC (train N=41 ExpR=-0.473, test N=9 ExpR=-0.232), XRP (train N=25 ExpR=-0.351, test N=9 ExpR=+0.032), BNB (train N=50 ExpR=-0.356, test N=7 ExpR=-0.553). Unlike many thin/ambiguous graveyard entries, the negative signal here sits on the LARGER (train) half specifically for every asset, with adequate sample size (25-50 trades) - not a small-N inconclusive result. Edge over a random-entry baseline within the same regime was also mixed-to-negative on most halves, giving no sign the elaborate breakout+retest timing mechanism is adding value beyond the regime filter alone. Not wired to live paper trading.
